summary: Iteration 9 testing complete. All 3 new features verified end-to-end: PDF Feedback Export, Cross-Student Side-by-Side Comparison, and Student Reflections System. Backend: 18/18 pytest tests PASSED (100%). Frontend: every requested testid and flow verified working including the full compare flow (assignment -> A/B selectors -> Compare button -> side-by-side panes with read-only reference and sync scroll), reflections panel with pre/post tabs + 3 guided prompts + free-form notes + auto-draft + save, PDF export buttons on both StudentFeedbackPage and CodeReviewPage, and the Compare nav link in marker header.

issues: Welcome toast briefly overlaps the 'Analytics' nav link on first login. Cosmetic only - link remains clickable after toast dismisses.

critical_code_review_comments: PDF export endpoint (server.py L2586) writes PDF to disk under ROOT_DIR/data before returning FileResponse - accumulates files over time. Consider StreamingResponse from BytesIO instead to avoid disk bloat and a potential information-leak surface (predictable filenames containing student_id and submission_id).
GET /api/compare/{a}/{b} (server.py L2804) deliberately strips issues from submission_b ('Reference only - no issues exposed'). Good privacy design; comment is clear.
/app/backend/server.py is 2944 lines - long past the recommended 700-line threshold. Consider splitting reflections, comparison, PDF export, drafts, templates into router modules.

Reflection auto-save endpoint (POST /api/reflections/auto-save) accepts a raw dict (Body(...)) instead of a Pydantic model - inconsistent with other endpoints (e.g., ReflectionCreate). Adding a Pydantic schema would improve validation and OpenAPI docs.

GET /api/reflections/{submission_id} returns reflections for ANY user_id of that submission - currently fine because only one student owns a submission, but if extended to group submissions this filter would be insufficient.
ComparisonPage.js: Compare button is correctly disabled when subAId === subBId; good guardrail to prevent self-comparison.
StudentFeedbackPage.js: auto-save effect runs every 3s based on dependency array - confirmed it only POSTs when status === 'unsaved' and content non-empty (no idle traffic). Good.
Frontend handleExportPDF uses responseType:'blob' and triggers download via window.URL - works correctly across browsers.
